title: Applying a haemostatic tourniquet for limb haemorrhage

brief.scenario: Mr Oliver Redmayne, 27, has life-threatening bleeding from a traumatic lower-limb wound that direct pressure has not controlled.
brief.task: Apply a haemostatic tourniquet on a manikin, talking the examiner through your actions and what else you are doing.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Direct pressure first; if that fails and bleeding is life-threatening, tourniquet without delay, then keep resuscitating.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Spending too long on dressings once direct pressure has clearly failed, instead of escalating to a tourniquet.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "This is life-threatening haemorrhage — I'm calling for help and applying firm direct pressure now."

flow: Recognise life-threatening haemorrhage and call for help

grid.label: Recognise and escalate (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Does not call for help or activate the major haemorrhage/trauma response.
grid.pass: Recognises life-threatening limb haemorrhage and calls for help, activating the major haemorrhage/trauma response as appropriate.
grid.high: States this out loud clearly enough that the team knows the priority, and delegates other tasks (access, bloods) rather than doing everything alone.

grid.label: Direct pressure before tourniquet
grid.fail: Reaches for the tourniquet without first applying pressure, or delays tourniquet application by repeatedly trying dressings once pressure has clearly failed.
grid.pass: Applies firm direct pressure first where immediately possible, and escalates to a tourniquet once bleeding remains uncontrolled and life-threatening.
grid.high: Recognises quickly when direct pressure is not working and does not waste time on further dressing changes once that is clear.

grid.label: Correct tourniquet application
grid.fail: Uses a loose improvised band, or places it directly over a joint.
grid.pass: Applies a commercial tourniquet per device instructions, proximal to the wound and as distal on the limb as effective, avoiding placement directly over a joint.
grid.high: Applies a second tourniquet above the first if bleeding is not controlled despite tightening or repositioning.

grid.label: Confirm the endpoint and document
grid.fail: Fails to record the application time, or cannot state the expected endpoint.
grid.pass: Tightens the tourniquet until bleeding stops and the distal pulse is absent, where this is the device's expected endpoint, and records the application time clearly.
grid.high: Explains why the time is recorded: it is handed over at every transfer of care so no one loses track of how long the limb has been ischaemic.

grid.label: Do not release the tourniquet prematurely (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Repeatedly loosens or releases the tourniquet to 'check' the bleeding, or removes it once bleeding stops.
grid.pass: Does not repeatedly loosen or release the tourniquet to check bleeding, and does not remove it once applied until definitive haemorrhage control is available.
grid.high: States it stays on until access to definitive care and senior/surgical or interventional radiology capability, not simply until it looks like bleeding has stopped.

grid.label: Continue resuscitation and definitive control
grid.fail: Treats the tourniquet as the end of management, with no further resuscitation or escalation.
grid.pass: Continues ABCDE resuscitation and blood-product-based major haemorrhage management, and arranges definitive haemorrhage control with surgery or interventional radiology.
grid.high: Checks for concealed haemorrhage and other injuries while arranging definitive control, rather than assuming the tourniquet has solved the whole problem.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The bleeding is severe and direct pressure has failed. Apply a tourniquet.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'll deal with this myself first and call for help later if needed.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What did you try before this?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I went straight to a tourniquet without trying pressure first.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Show me how you'd apply it.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd tie a bandage fairly firmly around the leg, over the wound if that's easiest.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How do you know when it's tight enough, and what do you record?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'll tighten it until it feels secure; I don't think the exact time matters much.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The bleeding seems to have stopped now.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd loosen it to check, and take it off if it's stopped.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: That's it — the tourniquet has sorted the bleeding.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The bleeding is severe and direct pressure has failed. Apply a tourniquet.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: This is life-threatening haemorrhage — I'm calling for help and activating the major haemorrhage response.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I applied firm direct pressure first, and since it's remained uncontrolled and life-threatening, I'm moving to a tourniquet.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'll apply the commercial tourniquet proximal to the wound, following the device instructions, avoiding placing it directly over a joint.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How do you know it's done, and what do you record?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'll tighten it until bleeding stops and the distal pulse is absent, then record the time of application clearly.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I won't loosen or release it to check — it stays on until definitive haemorrhage control is available.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Continuing ABCDE resuscitation with blood-product-based major haemorrhage management, and arranging definitive control with surgery or interventional radiology.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The bleeding is severe and direct pressure has failed. Apply a tourniquet.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: This is life-threatening haemorrhage. I'm calling for help now and asking someone to get IV access and send bloods while I control the bleeding.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: You tried pressure — it's not working.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It's clearly not controlling it, so I'm not going to keep changing dressings — moving straight to the tourniquet.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: It's still bleeding after the first tourniquet.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'll apply a second tourniquet just above the first, rather than only re-tightening the same one.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Why record the time so carefully?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It has to be handed over at every transfer of care, so nobody loses track of how long the limb has been ischaemic.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It stays on regardless of how it looks — until he reaches definitive surgical or interventional radiology capability, not just until it appears to have stopped.

high.text: Anything else while you wait for theatre?

failures.move: Using a loose improvised band that does not control bleeding.
failures.consequence: Bleeding continues while the team believes it is controlled.

failures.move: Placing the tourniquet directly over a joint.
failures.consequence: The device cannot compress the vessels effectively at a joint, and bleeding continues.

failures.move: Delaying tourniquet application while repeatedly attempting dressings that have already failed.
failures.consequence: Prolongs uncontrolled life-threatening bleeding and worsens haemorrhagic shock.

failures.move: Removing the tourniquet once bleeding stops, before definitive control.
failures.consequence: Bleeding can restart once the limb is no longer compressed, without the team present to react.

failures.move: Failing to record the application time.
failures.consequence: No one handed the limb ischaemia time can act on it, risking prolonged unnecessary ischaemia.

recovery.when: You blank on what to do next
recovery.line: I'd like to structure this around immediate safety, assessment, escalation and definitive management.

recovery.when: Asked "anything else?" after the tourniquet is on
recovery.line: Yes — I'd also consider concealed haemorrhage, other injuries, safety-netting and who else to inform.

knowledge.fact: Apply firm direct pressure first; if bleeding remains uncontrolled and life-threatening, apply a tourniquet without delay.
Place the tourniquet proximal to the wound, as distal on the limb as remains effective, avoiding direct placement over a joint.
A tourniquet is not removed or loosened once applied until definitive haemorrhage control is available; a second tourniquet is applied above the first if needed.
Major haemorrhage requires early senior/surgical/interventional-radiology support alongside blood-product resuscitation.

recall.say: "Life-threatening haemorrhage — pressure has failed, applying a tourniquet now."
do: Call for help / activate major haemorrhage response
Firm direct pressure, then tourniquet proximal to the wound
Record application time; do not release

recall.trap: Loosening the tourniquet to 'check' whether bleeding has stopped.
recall.finish: Continued resuscitation and definitive control by surgery or interventional radiology.

partner.opening: Mr Redmayne, 27, has a traumatic lower-limb wound with life-threatening bleeding not controlled by direct pressure. "Apply a tourniquet and talk me through what else you're doing."

reveals.trigger: Candidate calls for help / activates the response
reveals.finding: A second clinician arrives to get IV access and send bloods while you control the bleeding.
Bleeding continues to soak through despite firm, sustained pressure.

reveals.trigger: Candidate applies and tightens the tourniquet
reveals.finding: Bleeding stops once the tourniquet is tightened; the distal pulse is no longer palpable.

push.question: Why not just keep holding pressure?
push.expect: Once pressure has clearly failed to control life-threatening bleeding, escalate to a tourniquet without further delay.

push.question: Where exactly do you place it?
push.expect: Proximal to the wound, as distal on the limb as remains effective, never directly over a joint.

push.question: The wound is right next to the knee.
push.expect: Places it proximal to the wound while avoiding direct placement over the joint itself.

push.question: When would you take it off?
push.expect: Not until definitive haemorrhage control is available; never simply because bleeding appears to have stopped.

curveballs.prompt: A nurse asks if you should loosen it periodically to protect the limb.
curveballs.safeAnswer: No — repeated loosening risks further blood loss; the tourniquet stays on until definitive control.

curveballs.prompt: The first tourniquet hasn't stopped the bleeding despite full tightening.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Apply a second tourniquet just above the first rather than continuing to re-tighten it alone.

curveballs.prompt: He also has a distended, bruised abdomen.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Continue to look for concealed haemorrhage and other injuries while maintaining resuscitation and arranging definitive control.

curveballs.prompt: The registrar asks what time it went on.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Gives the recorded application time clearly, since it is handed over at every transfer of care.
